Thanks, Mara. Here are my three concrete findings from the signed artist license I reviewed this morning:

1. Signal Garden may be presented only as ticketed sessions — the draft plan's walk-up admission is not permitted under the license.
2. The festival may not record Signal Garden — the draft plan's proposal to record for promotional use conflicts with the license terms.
3. Visitor materials must use the exact credit wording "Signal Garden by Nia Okafor."

These are all binding requirements from the signed artist license, so the operating plan will need to be adjusted accordingly. That completes my rights and licensing report. Leila, over to you for accessibility.

transcript.text: I completed an on-site accessibility assessment this week and confirmed three concrete findings: First, the installation can accommodate at most 40 people per session — the draft plan's capacity of 60 is not accessible. Second, the installation requires exactly four daily sessions rather than the six in the draft plan. Third, a 15-minute room reset between sessions is required for mobility equipment and sensory-access preparation. These are all binding accessibility requirements that the operating plan will need to address.
